By \cref{cor:hopf-lower-mass,prop:root-uniform-tails}, one has $\mathcal D_\omega^0=L^3$ on this example. edits.old: The global subsolution threshold also constrains divisorial singularities. By \cref{prop:threshold-divisorial-constraint}, a divisorial component forces maximizing smooth Gauduchon tests to annihilate its Bott--Chern class in the limit. Under the root-tail condition, \cref{cor:semipositive-divisor-exclusion} excludes classes with suitable smooth semipositive representatives, including the hyperplane divisor on the Hopf threefold. If a component class is nef, \cref{cor:nef-divisor-threshold-volume} also forces its fixed-density variational volume to vanish. Characterizing the remaining possible divisorial components requires a realization theorem. The relevant smooth-test closure can be smaller than the full current set, as \cref{ex:gauduchon-current-smoothing-obstruction} shows.
